markdown_report:
The best next step is a controlled recent-context replacement probe for each category’s single HSTU. At 10% research progress, improving diagnostic specificity is more feasible than introducing an unverified architectural change. Replacement sensitivity must first survive controls for popularity and semantic disruption before motivating training changes.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) User feedback favors recent, specific connections. It motivates testing recent-context sensitivity but does not establish that stronger recency weighting improves HR@10. (2) Existing deletions change evidence and sequence geometry together. Holding occupied positions fixed reduces this ambiguity but leaves substitution-content effects. (3) Removing the last item changes the readout anchor. Preserve that item when investigating preceding context.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [HSTU](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152) combines unnormalized SiLU attention, relative biases, normalization, and multiplicative gating. Replacement changes their content-dependent computations; it cannot isolate any mechanism. (2) [Activation-patching guidance](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042) shows that corruption and output metrics affect localization. Use matched controls and report margins alongside ranks. (3) [CoSeRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.06479) motivates preserving meaningful sequence information during augmentation. Together with [negative-sampling research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276), this supports semantic and popularity controls without establishing full-catalog validity.

These insights define three directions: controlled context interventions, internal mechanism localization, and prospective validation of diagnostic predictions. A common framework separates **evidence changed**, **geometry preserved**, and **inference supported**:

| Probe | Evidence/geometry | Supported interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Existing deletion | Removed/changed | Joint content–position sensitivity |
| Proposed replacement | Substituted/preserved inputs | Policy-specific content sensitivity |
| Internal patching | Activation restored/controlled | Component-specific recovery |

Three atomic ideas merit consideration. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Matched recent-versus-random replacement | 5/7/5 | Useful control combination; reusable; needs no backbone changes | Established method; uncertain predictive validity; joint matching complicates implementation |
| Final-position gate patching | 7/7/7 | HSTU mechanism focus; useful localization; bounded intervention | Established patching; corruption-dependent; requires verified internal hooks |
| Jointly learned recency bias | 4/7/4 | Minimal hypothesis; direct training test; one network | Familiar mechanism; may suppress useful older interests; predictor serialization must change |

**Selected algorithm.** Reserve the last training interaction as target; retain its preceding item as the observed anchor. Score intact history against 99 fixed unique unseen negatives. Replace equal numbers of recent and uniformly sampled preceding items, preserving occupied positions, lengths, masks, timestamps, and anchor. Add a frequency-matched random-position control: otherwise differences between original recent and random items remain confounded with position.

Cross position controls with uniform, frequency-matched, and frequency-plus-text-similarity-matched replacement policies. Use training-only counts and TF–IDF titles/descriptions; no external embeddings. Couple substitution draws only where replacements satisfy both conditions’ matching constraints. Report unmatched users, missing text, residual imbalance, and subset overlap; compare policies on their common eligible users. Sweep replacement severity, include identity controls and within-history swaps, and repeat fixed corruption draws. Swaps preserve item counts but change transitions.

Report changes from intact predictions in target rank, HR@10, and target-versus-highest-negative margin, plus recent-minus-control differences. Average draws within users before paired bootstrap; these are in-sample, intervention-specific sensitivity measurements, not intent, component localization, or generalization estimates.

Retain `DiagnosisProbe`, metric definitions, interpreter, and ModelView interfaces. Read features at the greatest nonzero index. Keep four category models, routing, seeds, training limits, and host evaluation unchanged. Predeclare one subsequent HSTU training hypothesis and a matched control; record all attempts and judge them solely by host macro validation HR@10. Repeated validation selection risks [adaptive overfitting](https://arxiv.org/abs/1506.02629); bootstrap intervals do not correct it. Final held-out evaluation remains untouched during search, and sampled gains do not establish [full-catalog gains](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/).

idea.description: Extend the paired recent-versus-random replacement diagnostic with explicit controls for original-item popularity, substitute popularity, semantic disruption, and corruption severity. Each category continues to use exactly one independently trained HSTU.
idea.motivation: Deletion confounds evidence removal with sequence geometry, while uncontrolled replacement confounds position with the characteristics of replaced and substituted items. The revised protocol tests whether recent-position sensitivity persists across specified controls before proposing stronger recency weighting.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and all ModelView interfaces. Use view.model in evaluation mode under no_grad, restoring model mode and Python, NumPy, Torch CPU, and applicable CUDA RNG states in finally. Use local diagnostic seed 42; do not change preprocessing seed 0 or training seed 42. Select at most 200 eligible training users per category by sorting IDs and applying a seeded permutation. Reserve history[-1] as target; truncate history[:-1] to the existing model length and left-pad it. Keep the final observed item unchanged and read the greatest nonzero index. Require at least four preceding occupied positions. For m eligible positions, test k=max(1,floor(f*m)) for f in {0.1,0.3}, deduplicating identical k values. Recent positions are the last k positions before the anchor. Draw a uniform k-subset from all preceding positions and an additional k-subset matched to recent originals by floor(log2(training_count)) frequency bins. Allow overlap, report it, and skip infeasible matched cells without relaxing constraints silently. Build counts and TF–IDF vectors solely from training item IDs and available titles/descriptions, using word unigrams/bigrams, lowercase text, sublinear term frequency, and L2 normalization. Uniform replacements use real training items; frequency-matched replacements require the original item's frequency bin; semantic-matched replacements additionally require cosine similarity at least 0.2 to the original. Exclude the entire original user history, the target, sampled candidate IDs, and already selected substitutes. Generate the fixed 99 unique negatives uniformly from training items outside the user's entire training history; keep candidates identical across conditions and draws. For each paired position, sample one shared substitute uniformly from the intersection of its two admissible pools; mark empty intersections as unmatched. Shared draws therefore estimate sensitivity on common replacement support, rather than the full marginal policy. Report eligible counts, original-item count imbalance, substitute counts, cosine distributions, text coverage, overlap, and matching failures. Compare policies on their common eligible user set and also report policy-specific coverage. Use five corruption draws per cell, identity controls, and within-history swaps between selected positions and disjoint preceding positions, preserving the anchor. Cache clean and perturbed scores and aggregate draws within user. Define margin as target score minus maximum negative score; define rank using descending scores with item-ID tie breaking. Report raw score margins without cross-model scale comparisons. Bootstrap users 2,000 times within category, retaining all their conditions together; report percentile 95% intervals. Recompute equally weighted four-category differences for every replicate only when all four category results are available. In-sample intervals condition on fitted models, fixed candidates, and the corruption design. Identity controls should reproduce clean scores within numerical tolerance. Diagnostic-only changes need no checkpoint or predictor architecture changes. Any subsequent learned recency feature must remain inside one jointly trained HSTU and be serialized consistently in both training and the predictor writer. Preserve DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, routing, single-GPU execution, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, and the shared search budget. Predeclare the diagnostic prediction, one intervention, a matched control, and the validation comparison rule; retain unsuccessful attempts. Do not infer compatibility, purchase intent, or unobserved traits from text similarity.
idea.pseudocode:
save model mode and Python/NumPy/Torch/CUDA RNG states
try:
    set view.model.eval(); disable gradients
    initialize local diagnostic RNG(seed=42)
    compute training-only counts, frequency bins, and TF-IDF item vectors
    select up to 200 eligible users per category using fixed seeded ordering
    for user:
        target = history[-1]
        context = left_pad(truncate(history[:-1], existing_max_length))
        anchor = greatest_nonzero_index(context)
        preceding = occupied positions strictly before anchor
        candidates = fixed target + 99 unique training-item negatives unseen in full history
        clean = score(context, candidates, readout=anchor)
        cache identity-control scores
        for distinct k from fractions {0.1, 0.3}:
            recent = final k preceding positions
            for draw in range(5):
                uniform_control = uniform k-subset of preceding
                matched_control = k-subset with same original frequency-bin counts as recent
                record overlap and matching coverage
                for control in available controls:
                    pair recent/control positions deterministically within frequency bins where applicable
                    for policy in {uniform, frequency, frequency_plus_semantic}:
                        build admissible substitute pools for both originals in each pair
                        intersect pools; exclude history, candidates, and selected substitutes
                        if any intersection is empty: record unmatched cell; continue
                        sample shared substitutes from intersections
                        replace items in place for recent and control conditions
                        score both with unchanged anchor and candidates
                        cache clean-relative margin, rank, HR@10, and top-10 overlap
                construct anchor-preserving within-history swap controls and score
    aggregate corruption draws within user
    compare policies on common eligible users; report coverage and residual imbalance
    bootstrap users within category, keeping all paired conditions together
    if all four category outputs exist: recompute macro differences per bootstrap replicate
    return {'metrics': measured_results, 'metric_definitions': explicit_definitions}
finally:
    restore model mode and all saved RNG states

diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    include measured metrics, definitions, coverage, uncertainty, and limitations
    request evidence-supported findings and one prospective training hypothesis
    prohibit interpreting sensitivity as user intent or isolated HSTU mechanism

originality.positive: Combines anchor preservation, original-item matching, shared-support substitutions, and semantic controls within the HSTU diagnostic contract.
originality.negative: Perturbation, matching, and robustness controls are established methods; the contribution is a task-specific diagnostic protocol.

future_potential.positive: Creates a reusable basis for prospectively testing whether controlled diagnostic signals predict useful single-model HSTU interventions.
future_potential.negative: Results may depend strongly on replacement support and in-sample fitting; four categories provide limited evidence of predictive validity.

code_difficulty.positive: Existing feature and scoring interfaces suffice, without retraining or internal activation hooks.
code_difficulty.negative: Joint matching, sparse semantic retrieval, missingness accounting, coupled draws, and paired aggregation require more engineering than the original proposal acknowledged.

related_work.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU mechanisms including pointwise SiLU attention, relative attention biases, and multiplicative gating.
limitations: Does not establish which mechanisms the supplied implementation exposes or that recent-context sensitivity predicts recommendation quality.
Input replacement changes multiple content-dependent computations simultaneously.

related_work.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
contributions: Examines how corruption choices and output metrics affect intervention-based localization.
limitations: Does not directly validate recommendation-specific perturbations or interpretations of user intent.

related_work.title: Prakash et al. (2024), negative-sampling study supplied in the research context
contributions: Motivates examining interactions between negative sampling and item-popularity distributions.
limitations: Popularity matching is a diagnostic control and does not guarantee full-catalog evaluation validity.

related_work.title: CoSeRec: Contrastive Learning for Sequential Recommendation with Robust Augmentation
contributions: Motivates correlated-item augmentation to reduce damage to meaningful sequence information.
limitations: Does not establish that TF–IDF similarity preserves functional relevance or that the proposed diagnostic identifies recency mechanisms.

related_work.title: Cascade-guided Adversarial Training, supplied research context
contributions: Investigates temporal reliance and robustness to real-item replacements.
limitations: Replacement sensitivity alone cannot establish beneficial recency weighting or causal user preference.

related_work.title: Krichene and Rendle: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking evaluation can yield model comparisons inconsistent with full-catalog evaluation.
limitations: Does not change the mandated benchmark; sampled HR@10 remains the selection criterion here.

related_work.title: Dwork et al.: The Reusable Holdout—Preserving Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis
contributions: Explains how adaptive reuse of evaluation data can undermine statistical validity.
limitations: Logging hypotheses and limiting queries reduce opportunities for selection bias but do not themselves provide a formal correction.
